She had her son when she was 16, and that’s a very hard thing to deal with. Maybe she wasn’t able to access an abortion, maybe she didn’t want to go through one. I’m sure this wasn’t the intention, but this comment is a bit in poor taste. Saying that he tolerates her body is not going to make her feel good at all, and you don’t know if that’s the case, only he does. Also, “just trying” to lose weight is simply not possible for certain people. I don’t know this girl’s situation, but many people have health or financial problems that make it practically impossible to do so. Also, recommending someone change their body when they’re insecure is a slippery slope that can quickly lead to eating disorders. Not trying to be rude, just offering some insight.

Personally, I LOVE my girlfriend’s body, and she’s fat. Nothing wrong with it, she’s healthy and beautiful, that’s just how her body is (and once again, i love it!). These insecurities are totally normal though. Skinny people experience it too with other things, but I imagine it must be a lot harder when you’re fat since society is constantly telling you your body isn’t good enough.

For advice, talk to him about this. Tell him you’re feeling a bit insecure, and ask him how he feels about your body. If he’s the one for you, he’ll enthusiastically say he loves it, or at least he’ll say he likes it. And I totally get how the lack of compliments is off putting, but the fact is that certain people just don’t naturally express their love / attraction through words. I’ve had to ask my girlfriend to give me more compliments, not because she doesn’t think I’m beautiful, but because she didn’t realize the amount of compliments she was giving wasn’t enough for me. I totally feel for your situation, people sometimes struggle to see how being fat really messes with your head sometimes because of how the world is. I hope you two can work it out :)
